messages:
devon: heads-up — seeing a surge of node join failures in ap-southeast-1 since the firewall cutover at 08:03 UTC. GPU warm pool struggling to reach target capacity. alert: https://incidents.redwood/INC-3821 :alarm_clock:
ops-bot: [ALERT] node-register-failed ap-southeast-1 x23x — 87 failures in 12m — impacted service: warm-pool-autoscaler
devon: example log from node:
```
keystore: decrypt failed: AccessDenied (403) for kms:Decrypt
audit-shipper: PutObject -> 403 Forbidden to s3://redwood-audit-ap-southeast
service-agent: registration timeout talking to keystore endpoint
```
lina: ugh. sounds like egress to S3 + KMS endpoints blocked by the new default-deny egress rules. which change rolled?
devon: fw rollout PR #917 landed 08:02 UTC. rule set tightened to deny all egress except known endpoints. looks like keystore and audit-shipper endpoints didn't make the allowlist (they're behind private endpoints + NATs).
harry: confirming — policy change was intended to remove broad natgw access. we scoped allowlist to cloud-platform endpoints but missed the ephemeral keystore hostnames in ap-southeast. my bad.
sec-jen: impact = nodes can't decrypt boot tokens (KMS) and can't ship audit logs (S3). both will block registration and trigger retries — warm pool stays underprovisioned => perf + cost (retries).
lina: temporary mitigation options?
devon: quick fixes I can push now:
1) add VPC endpoint for S3 in the affected subnets (aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint ...)
2) OR add temporary egress SG rule to allow keystore CIDR range we have in inventory (10.34.128.0/22) for 2 hours
3) rollback FW policy to previous rule-set (breaks the hardening)
(2) is fastest to unblock while we get endpoint in place.
harry: KMS key policy might also block cross-account decrypt if endpoint path changes. we should check key's Condition for aws:SourceVpc or SourceIp.
devon: checked — key policy is fine, but KMS requests are coming from nodes via privnet proxy; the proxy's egress IP differs when we hit natgw vs privatelink; that's why AccessDenied shows.
sec-jen: recommended path: do not rollback. implement VPC endpoint for S3 + add precise SG allowlist for keystore IPs as a timeboxed canary (60m). then update infra-as-code to include keystore/shipper endpoints and run canary. If KMS policy needs tweak, we do a targeted change with approval.
lina: +1. I can do the SG allowlist now and monitor. devon — can you create the endpoint canary? put steps here.
devon: doing. quick commands I'll run (ap-southeast-1):
```
# create S3 interface endpoint in the warm-pool subnets
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint --vpc-id vpc-0a1b2c3d --service-name com.amazonaws.ap-southeast-1.s3 --vpc-endpoint-type Interface --subnet-ids subnet-aaa,subnet-bbb --security-group-ids sg-warmpool --region ap-southeast-1
# temp SG rule (60m) to allow keystore IP block
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-warmpool --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.34.128.0/22 --region ap-southeast-1
```
devon: also adding CloudWatch filter for the 403s and a synthetic node registration metric to track recovery.
lina: done with the SG rule — added 10.34.128.0/22 egress for 60m, tagged with "temp-keystore-unblock-176945". monitoring now.
ops-bot: [CHANGE] SecurityGroup sg-warmpool modified by lina — change-id sgchg-9991 — expiry: 60m
harry: I also pushed a note to KMS owners to check key usage logs — if we see requests from unexpected sourceIP we may need to update key Condition to allow the privnet proxy IP pool.
sec-jen: action items: 
- devon: deploy S3 endpoint canary (in progress)
- harry: validate KMS key Condition and propose minimal update if needed (ETA 30m)
- lina: monitor warm-pool registration and revoke SG rule after stable (or extend with approvals)
- ops: open follow-up infra-as-code PR to persist endpoints + update firewall allowlist
can we set a target for recovery?
lina: if SG fix + endpoint goes green within 10m we should see node join rate back to normal; otherwise escalate to rollback.
devon: endpoint created (canary) — routing propagated, DNS resolving to endpoint IPs. starting registration spike check.
ops-bot: [METRIC] warm-pool target=50 current=12 -> 35 after 120s since SG change
lina: nice, joining trend looks good. keep eyes on audit-shipper errors.
devon: audit PutObject 403s decreased by 90% after endpoint. KMS decrypt errors reduced to <5/min.
sec-jen: great. leave the SG rule until we merge infra-as-code and deploy endpoint to all subnets. then we revoke the temp rule.
harry: I'll draft the minimal KMS condition change if logs show missing SourceVpc. will post PR for review.
lina: final note: cost impact — retries + warm pool partials added ~0.6 GPU-hours wasted in last hour (~$12). logged to INC-3821.
devon: closing loop: will follow up with PRs: vpc-endpoints.tf + firewall-allowlist.tf + runbook update for keystore endpoint checklist. thanks team 
harry: thanks all :thumbsup:
sec-jen: nice recovery — please keep the timeline and config diffs in the incident ticket.
ops-bot: [INCIDENT] INC-3821 status -> mitigated (temporary allowlist + endpoint canary)
